chunks: It was said to Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon them both): What is death?

He said: It is the sleep that comes to you every night, except that its duration is long and one will not awaken from it except on the Day of Resurrection. Who has seen in his sleep from the types of happiness what he cannot evaluate its value, and from the types of horrors what he cannot evaluate its value? How is the case of happiness and dread during sleep? That is death, so prepare for it.
ai.seo_question: How does Shia tradition define death in relation to sleep?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this profound analogy from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him), who likens death to a prolonged sleep characterized by the intense, inescapable mix of joy and awe experienced during dreams. This comparison underscores the transient nature of worldly consciousness and serves as a spiritual exhortation for believers to prepare for the permanent awakening on the Day of Resurrection. The narration highlights the continuity of the soul's experience between the minor death of sleep and the major death of the grave.
